solute-potential-formula.def: The formula-sheet equation for solute potential: Ψs = −iCRT, where i is the ionization constant, C the molar concentration, R the pressure constant and T the temperature in kelvin.

ionization-constant.def: In Ψs = −iCRT, i is the number of particles each formula unit makes when it dissolves: 1 for sucrose or glucose (they do not ionize), about 2 for NaCl (Na⁺ + Cl⁻), about 3 for CaCl₂.

molar-concentration.def: Moles of solute per liter of solution (mol/L, written M). A 0.2 M sucrose solution has 0.2 mol of sucrose in each liter.

pressure-constant.def: In Ψs = −iCRT, R = 0.0831 L·bar/(mol·K). It converts concentration and temperature into a pressure in bars.

kelvin.def: The absolute temperature scale used in Ψs = −iCRT: kelvin = °C + 273. Room temperature, 22 °C, is 295 K.

bar-unit.def: A unit of pressure used for water potential; 1 bar is about atmospheric pressure at sea level. 10 bars = 1 megapascal (MPa), the unit many textbooks use.

wp-calculation.def: Finding water potential with Ψ = ΨP + Ψs: calculate Ψs = −iCRT, add the pressure potential (0 in an open container), and compare values; water moves from higher (less negative) to lower (more negative) Ψ.
